lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Make the portfolio link a direct, working URL to relevant work.
items.because: A repository or project page is more useful than a broad profile.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is irrelevant to engineering qualifications and can introduce unnecessary bias.

items.says: Remove nationality unless it is specifically requested.
items.because: Nationality is not the same as work authorization and may create avoidable screening concerns.

items.says: Add a concise professional headline or summary.
items.because: The reader currently has to infer the target role from the experience and skills.

items.says: Clarify the status of the expected graduation date.
items.because: It should remain current and not imply the degree is already completed.

items.says: Make the institution’s city and country identifiable.
items.because: The supplied location labels are generic, especially for readers unfamiliar with the institution.

items.says: Make the institution’s city and country identifiable.
items.because: The supplied location labels are generic, especially for readers unfamiliar with the institution.

items.says: Consider whether both education locations need to be listed.
items.because: They take space if they do not clarify where you studied or matter to the role.

items.says: Define diagnostic accuracy and clarify the 35% change, evaluation set, and baseline.
items.because: The reader cannot assess the result’s size or reliability without those details.

items.says: Explain how reviewer disagreement was measured and over what sample.
items.because: The measurement needs context.

items.says: Show that lower disagreement reflected better review outcomes.
items.because: Greater agreement could instead suppress valid differences.

items.says: Clarify how equal accuracy was established and the scope of the evaluation.
items.because: The reader needs to judge how robust the comparison is.

items.says: Clarify whether the latency reduction is relative or absolute.
Clarify when the regressions were found and how the harness affected release decisions.
items.because: That would make the impact more concrete than saying it caught two regressions.

items.says: The fine-tuning method repeats the first internship bullet.
items.because: The first bullet already describes adapter fine-tuning with assistant-only loss masking.

items.says: Clarify which assistant-generated and tool-output tokens received training loss.
items.because: The stated learning objective leaves a technical reader unsure.

items.says: Consider moving the diagnostics triage outcome earlier in the experience section.
items.because: It is one of the most compelling outcomes.

items.says: Clarify the backlog baseline, measurement period, and meaning of the 800+ signals figure.
items.because: The impact needs clearer measurement context.

items.says: The backlog achievement is duplicated in the Research-Agent Evaluation Framework project.
items.because: The repeated work blurs its attribution.

items.says: Specify the GPU-memory measure and workload behind the 4× reduction.
items.because: GPU memory can refer to several different measures.

items.says: Clarify the workload or test conditions behind the latency figures.
items.because: Those conditions give the figures context.

items.says: Distinguish the build-failing threshold from the achieved latency.
items.because: The threshold was an automated regression guard.

items.says: Correct the switch from past to present tense in the CI bullet.
items.because: The bullet describes past work but says “adds.”

items.says: Define the three-day release-cycle measure and its comparison baseline.
items.because: The reader needs to interpret the claimed improvement.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the team’s overall release process.
Quantify the backlog or dispatch delay eliminated if a defensible measure is available.
items.because: This outcome is less quantified than the others.

items.says: Ensure the outcome describes the migration’s demonstrable effect.
items.because: It should not imply more than you can demonstrate.

items.says: Replace or remove the generic AI-first engineering practices bullet.
items.because: Its claims about adoption, acceleration, and outcomes identify no specific system change or measurable result.

items.says: Explain the 100× comparison and how the context limit was measured.
items.because: The starting point and meaning of “raw conversation grew 100x” are unclear.

items.says: Add scope or test conditions for the 50-way fan-out if available.
Explain how elimination of deadlocks and lost results was verified.
items.because: “Removing” is a strong claim that needs supporting evidence.

items.says: Clarify whether you implemented the metrics, integrated existing implementations, or both.
items.because: Those represent different levels of ownership for a contributor.

items.says: Explain what the Kendall correlation was calculated against and what the trials consisted of.
items.because: The validation result is hard to judge without an explicit comparison.

items.says: The internship’s backlog achievement is repeated under an unrelated research-agent project.
items.because: The duplication makes the work’s attribution unclear.

items.says: Broaden the skills section with substantiated tools and capabilities already shown elsewhere.
items.because: The current list is unusually short relative to the experience and omits some described engineering work.

items.says: Make the “ML & Agents” category easier to scan.
items.because: It combines frameworks, methods, and a broad capability.
